name: SN65HVD230
full_name: Texas Instruments SN65HVD230 3.3-V CAN Bus Transceiver
description: The SN65HVD230 is the de-facto 3.3 V high-speed CAN physical-layer transceiver, sitting between a CAN controller's digital TXD/RXD lines and the differential CANH/CANL bus. It is a PHY only: it does not implement the CAN protocol, so it must be paired with a controller such as the MCP2515 or an MCU's built-in CAN/TWAI peripheral (ESP32, STM32). It runs from a single 3.3 V supply, tolerates a -2 V to 7 V bus common-mode range, withstands +/-25 V common-mode transients, and supports up to 120 nodes thanks to high input impedance. Its standout trait is the RS pin offering three modes in one part - full-speed switching, resistor-programmable slope control for EMI reduction, and a low-current (370 uA) listen-only standby - which is why nearly every 3.3 V MCU CAN project ships on the blue 'VP230' breakout board.

pins.name: D
pins.description: Driver (CAN transmit) data input, also called TXD; LOW for dominant and HIGH for recessive bus states. Connects to the controller's TXD line.

pins.name: R
pins.description: Receiver (CAN receive) data output, also called RXD; LOW for dominant and HIGH for recessive bus states. Connects to the controller's RXD line.

pins.name: Vref
pins.description: VCC/2 reference voltage output, useful for biasing split-termination common mode.

pins.name: RS
pins.description: Mode select: tie to GND for high-speed mode, add a resistor to GND (e.g. 10 kohm ~= 15 V/us, 100 kohm ~= 2 V/us) for slope control, or apply a high level for low-current standby (listen-only) mode.

typical_application: 3.3 V CAN node: MCU/DSP CAN controller (or MCP2515) drives D/R, transceiver drives a 120-ohm-terminated CANH/CANL twisted pair. Standard wiring on the VP230 breakout for ESP32/STM32 CAN/TWAI projects.
gotchas: This is a transceiver (PHY) only, not a CAN controller - it needs an MCP2515 or an MCU with a built-in CAN/TWAI controller to actually frame messages.
3.3 V part: do not substitute for the 5 V MCP2551/TJA1050 without checking supply; conversely it interoperates on the same bus with 5 V transceivers because CAN is differential.
RS (pin 8) must be handled - leave it floating and slope/mode behavior is undefined; tie to GND for normal high-speed operation.
Bus still needs proper 120-ohm termination at both physical ends of the trunk; the chip does not terminate the bus.
Low-power replacement for the PCA82C250, but at 3.3 V logic levels rather than 5 V.
